red_flags: Charging >$15/LF labor for chain link (should be $3.50-7/LF)
Charging >$15/LF labor for basic wood fence (should be $6-12/LF)
Requiring 'special' concrete mix when standard 60lb bags work fine
Claiming all posts need steel reinforcement (rarely necessary for residential)
Pushing premium cedar when treated pine would work equally well
Charging separately for 'measuring' or 'site visit' (should be included)
Requiring full fence replacement when partial repair would work
Claiming you need building permits for standard residential fence (check local codes - usually <6ft doesn't need permit)
Insisting on 3ft deep post holes when 2ft sufficient in most areas
Adding 'mobilization fee' >$200 for standard residential job
Charging >$500 for basic walk gate (should be $200-450 for wood)
Claiming soil conditions require drilling when standard auger works
Bundling staining/sealing at inflated prices (easy DIY or separate quote)

common_upsells.premium_posts: Steel posts when wood posts sufficient
common_upsells.premium_concrete: Special concrete mix vs. standard 60lb bags
common_upsells.unnecessary_gates: Adding extra gates you don't need
common_upsells.immediate_staining: Staining at install when fence should dry 6-12 months first
common_upsells.cedar_upgrade: Cedar fence when treated pine would work
common_upsells.vinyl_upgrade: Vinyl when you're on a budget and wood would work
common_upsells.decorative_elements: Post caps, lattice tops, fancy finials that add cost
common_upsells.privacy_slats: Chain link privacy slats when privacy fence would be similar cost

cost_factors.terrain: Sloped or uneven terrain increases labor 20-40%
cost_factors.access: Poor access requiring hand-digging increases cost 30-50%
cost_factors.soil_conditions: Rocky soil or hardpan adds $15-40/post for drilling
cost_factors.property_line_survey: May need $300-800 survey to locate exact boundaries
cost_factors.hoa_approval: Some HOAs restrict materials/colors, factor in approval time
cost_factors.local_codes: Height restrictions, setback requirements vary by municipality
cost_factors.seasonal: Winter installation may cost 10-20% more in cold climates

regional_notes.frost_line: Northern climates require deeper post holes (below frost line, typically 36-48 inches)
regional_notes.hurricane_zones: Coastal areas may require additional bracing and deeper posts
regional_notes.hoa_common: Planned communities often have strict fence regulations
regional_notes.material_availability: Cedar more expensive in areas where it's not regionally sourced
regional_notes.labor_rates: Urban areas 20-40% higher labor than rural

maintenance_guidance.wood_fence: Restain/reseal every 2-3 years, inspect for rot annually, expect repairs after 10-15 years
maintenance_guidance.vinyl_fence: Minimal maintenance, wash annually, check posts for stability
maintenance_guidance.chain_link: Inspect for rust spots, tighten fabric if sagging, lubricate gates
maintenance_guidance.aluminum_fence: Very low maintenance, occasional washing, check hardware
maintenance_guidance.wrought_iron: Requires regular rust prevention, repainting every 5-10 years
